title: Towards a Recognition System for the Mexican Sign Language: Arm Movement Detection
content: This paper describes ongoing work in the creation of a recognition system for the Mexican Sign Language (LSM). We propose a general sign decomposition into three parts: hand configuration (HC), arm movement (AM) and non-hand gestures (NHG). This paper focuses on the AM features and reports the approach created to analyze visual patterns in arm joint movements (wrists, shoulders and elbows). For this research, a proprietary dataset —that do not limit the recognition of arm movements— was developed, with active participation from the deaf community and LSM experts. We conduct analysis on two case studies of three sign subsets. For each sign, the pose was extracted to generate shapes of the joint paths during the arm movements and feeded to a CNN classifier. YOLOv8 was used for pose estimation and visual patterns classification purposes. The proposed approach, based on pose estimation, shows promising results for constructing CNN models to classify a wide range of signs.
